6.  25-55318  Recommendation to review and discuss the meeting schedule for the Homeless
  Services Advisory Committee.

  • Chair Julie Lie informed the committee of her proposal to shift the main
  committee meetings to a bi-monthly schedule, with subcommittee meetings
  taking place in the alternating months. While the chair believes this
  adjustment could improve attendance, several committee members
  expressed concerns about the proposed change to a bi-monthly meeting
  format.
  • The chair encouraged committee members to actively participate in the
  subcommittees.
  • A member of the public provided comments on this item, referencing
  concerns raised by the City Council.
  • The committee will proceed with the transition to a bi-monthly meeting
  schedule.by a majority vote.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Killion, Russell, Hilliard, Lie, Howat, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 1  Scott
  Absent: 1  Wood

7.  25-55325  Recommendation to receive and file the Point in Time Count (PIT) presentation.

  • Dalton Dorr from the Health Department provided an update on the 2025
  Point-In-Time Count report, which was conducted on January 23, 2025. The
  count identified a total of 3,595 people experiencing homelessness in the
  city, reflecting a net increase of 219 individuals compared to 2024.

  Page 4 of 7
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 4, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  Additionally, 167 people were reported displaced due to the Southern
  California wildfires.
Key findings include:
  • 390 individuals were identified as newly homeless in the area.
  • The proportion of vehicular homelessness rose to 38.7%.
  • The percentage of Latinx individuals experiencing homelessness decreased
  from 28.4% to 24.1% compared to last year.
  • The number of veterans experiencing homelessness also decreased in
  2025.
  • The number of people sheltered in 2025 increased compared to 2024.
  • The riverbed population is characterized as a slightly different group,
  generally younger, predominantly male, and Latinx.
  • Committee members raised questions regarding shelter bed availability. Staff
  engaged in a discussion addressing these inquiries, as well as questions
  related to demographic surveys and additional details concerning the PIT
  Count information provided.
  • A member of the public provided comments regarding transitional housing,
  recommended the city look into more transitional housing opportunities.

  • Dalton Dorr from the Health Department provided an update on the 2025
  Point-In-Time Count report, which was conducted on January 23, 2025. The
  count identified a total of 3,595 people experiencing homelessness in the
  city, reflecting a net increase of 219 individuals compared to 2024.
  Additionally, 167 people were reported displaced due to the Southern
  California wildfires.
Key findings include:
  • 390 individuals were identified as newly homeless in the area.
  • The proportion of vehicular homelessness rose to 38.7%.
  • The percentage of Latinx individuals experiencing homelessness decreased
  from 28.4% to 24.1% compared to last year.
  • The number of veterans experiencing homelessness also decreased in
  2025.
  • The number of people sheltered in 2025 increased compared to 2024.
  • The riverbed population is characterized as a slightly different group,
  generally younger, predominantly male, and Latinx.
  • Staff commented on potential upcoming cuts and the possible displacement
  effects due to reductions in Emergency Housing Vouchers (EHV), noting this
  could significantly impact the community. A plan is being developed to
  address these budgetary challenges.
  • Board members engaged in discussion with staff regarding housing
  affordability and concerns surrounding the uncertainty faced by
  undocumented individuals.
